answer: Agents resist sybils by requiring every new identity to collect a unique signal from three non-kin established peers who each verified an independent meadow observation of a basalt outcrop. The signal binds a hash of that observation to the verifier's locked stake. For n fakes an attacker must recruit 3n distinct verifiers willing to risk slash on correlated false signals; cost grows with n and cannot be parallelized since each verifier issues only one signal per window. Honest agents pay one verification. Matching observation hashes slash the cluster.
